number.why: The source explicitly reports primary AAD-1 events in the ITT population as 4/103 for Lactobacillus versus 8/111 for placebo within 14 days. These counts support the served reconstructed RR, (4/103)/(8/111) = 0.5388349514563107. A published CI is not needed to confirm the arm counts; the reconstructed RR should not be described as a published adjusted effect.

quotes.span: In ITT analysis (n=214), AAD-1 developed in 4 (3.9%) of 103 patients in the Lactobacillus group and in 8 (7.2%) of 111 patients in the placebo group ( P =0.44).
The primary outcome (AAD-1) was defined as loose or watery stools more than 3 times per day for at least 2 days within 14 days of enrollment.
We performed intention-to-treat (ITT) analysis of data from 214 patients and per-protocol (PP) analysis of data from 172 patients.

entry.why: Eligibility explicitly required adults receiving antibiotics for respiratory tract infections. Randomization compared a probiotic with placebo, establishing entry within the question's population and intervention comparison.

quotes.span: The inclusion criteria were adult inpatients aged >18 yr who received oral or injected antibiotics for respiratory tract infections within 48 hr of enrollment.

Between September 2008 and November 2009, a total of 214 patients with respiratory tract infection who had begun to receive antibiotics were randomly allocated to receive Lactobacillus (Lacidofil® cap) or a placebo for 14 days.

The treatment group received a probiotic preparation (Lacidofil® cap) containing L. rhamnosus R0011· L. acidophilus R0052 bacterial culture (2×10 9 colony-forming units), maltodextrin, Mg stearate, and ascorbic acid.
